description: An ordinary web link reopens at its own URL with no earlier page history; a forwarded port keeps its reload semantics. The runner only launches the chat; the reopen, cookie and shared-cache checks are driven by scripts/app/android_link_reopen_check.py against a local HTTP server, and the rest is by hand.
automatedCoverage: Runner: launching the chat proves nothing about page history. JVM: ChatWebViewPoolTest, ChatLinkReopenTest and ChatLinkWebSlotTest use Robolectric shadows (the WebView feature probes fixed to unsupported) and prove which view instance the pool hands out, destroys and creates, not what a real renderer keeps. Device helper: `android_link_reopen_check.py reopen`, `cookie` and `cache` (see localServer) assert history.length, response sequence, request timestamps, preservation of the originally issued session and whether a unique cacheable script returns to the server.

localServer.description: Run `python3 scripts/app/android_link_reopen_check.py serve` on the host (on an emulator add `--host 127.0.0.1`); the links it prints carry the placeholder name persona.test, never this computer's address, so a capture shows no real network address. Make the name resolve first: `map-host --serial <serial>` points it at the emulator's alias for the host for the WebView of a debuggable emulator, then restart the app; it is not an adb reverse, so the link still takes the ordinary-link path. On a real phone use a hosts entry or a local DNS name instead. Each `serve` starts a fresh request log. Use an Agent reply for /a when checking first-open preload. Send /login, /whoami and /cache as the user's own messages so the session echo cannot be preloaded before login and the first cache asset request is observable. Then run `reopen`, `cookie` and `cache` with the phone's serial, the printed base (http://persona.test:<port>) and the log path.

pages./a: Shows `page=a load=<request sequence> history=<history.length>` and a link to /b; never cached
pages./b: Same state line for page b, with a link back to /a
pages./login: Issues one random session only on its first request, then redirects to /a; later release preloads cannot reissue or rotate it
pages./whoami: Shows the exact session value, or missing, and the response sequence that produced it
pages./cache: A no-store main document with one unique cacheable JavaScript subresource; the page shows its main response sequence after the script executes
pages./cache-asset.js: Cache-Control public,max-age=3600; a new random query key per server run makes its first network request mandatory

steps: Receive an Agent reply containing the /a link and wait for the list to stop scrolling
Read the server log, then tap the link
manualScenes.expect: The log has a request for /a before the tap (timestamps), and the card shows the page already loaded. No request count is asserted: a cache can answer a load without one.

steps: Open /a, go to /b, shrink the card to Peek and expand it again
Select text on a page and use AI edit, then Use as context
manualScenes.expect: Peek does not reload the page. The first Back returns to /a, the second closes the card. The selection actions carry the same context content as before.

steps: Run a dev server on the computer and tap its localhost link in an Agent reply
Change a served file, close the card and tap the link again
With the card open, edit a file that triggers hot reload
Stop the server and tap the link
manualScenes.expect: The reopened port shows the new content. Hot reload keeps working while the card is open. A stopped server reports the 404 notice as before. Not observable here and not claimed: that the phone's own loopback receives no request.

steps: Open a Feishu document link with the Lark extension on: the native reader shows, no page is loaded
Choose Open as web page, close and reopen
Kill the page's renderer process from adb on a web link and tap Reload
manualScenes.expect: The reader shows without a WebView until switched; after the switch a closed page reopens fresh. A killed renderer shows the quit notice and Reload builds a new view. If the renderer cannot be killed safely, report it as not verified on device.

asserts: the reopened page's history.length is 1 (no in-page history from page B)
the reopened page is a different load than the first one
that load is a logged /a request made after the card closed
no /b request after the card closed
reportedNotJudged: whether the reopened page's request came before or after the tap (a prerendered page is loaded again when opened)

asserts: the server issues exactly one random session; subsequent /login release preloads do not issue another
two distinct /whoami responses produced after login both return the originally issued session
a response produced before login, a missing or replaced session, and two openings showing the same response all fail
the reopened no-store main document is a new logged response
the unique cacheable script executes on both openings but reaches the server only on the first load
a second script request fails the check
reportedNotJudged: whether the shared HTTP cache is resident in memory or persisted on disk; process-restart disk persistence is not asserted

notVerified: How many WebView renderer processes exist (Chromium shares renderers by site, so the count does not follow the number of views).
That the phone's own loopback received no request for a forwarded port (nothing counts requests there).
How many requests one reopen makes: the preload happens when the card closes and the cache mode may answer a load without a request.
Whether the cookie store and HTTP cache survive an app process restart; the device checks cover release and preload within one process, not persistent storage across processes.
